posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
the makers are developed over time, with newer makers usually having more features and being easier to use. As such both 2K and 2K3 are rather old and restricted in their use (scripting was only introduced with RMXP, and they replaced scripts with the plugin API only on MV).
Without scripting you cannot change any part of the engine, which means both 2K/2K3 are limited to the type of game they were originally intended to produce, which was already said above.
Since this is likely a problem of the newer makers being too expensive for you, I suggest you regularly check

posts.author: Akkari
posts.body:
For me, a good rule of thumb for the two versions goes as follows:
Get RPG Maker 2000 if you want to make the smallest game possible exported to a Windows EXE that will work on modern Windows while still using an engine with a gui editor(yes, there is quite literally no current engine afaik that can beat RPG Maker 2000's blank project executable size that can run on Windows 10 and 11).
Else, just get RPG Maker 2003 and patch it to maniacs(maniacs patch is worth it just for the show string picture command, ogg support, updated exe, allowing 24/32bit images and the ability to change the resolution to whatever you want). Also, doing frontview battles will require a little bit of extra effort, but shouldn't be too hard to implement in RPG Maker 2003, unless I'm mistaken, it's one of the more basic customisations you can do to the battle system.
Basically, current RPG Maker 2003 patched to maniacs brings the old engine into the modern era with only a few hold overs left that show it's age.
Although RPG Maker 2003 patched to maniacs thrives on giving the user the tools through eventing to create their own systems(maniacs only expands on the toolset RPG Maker 2003 gave you), meanwhile the goal for Scripts in XP-VX/VXACE and Plugins in MV/MZ is to create the systems for you.
So I hard disagree with Andar here, while yes, it's definitely harder and more tedious due to what I mentioned above(tools over systems), it's extremely possible to do ALOT with it, thx to the said tools(and way more possible thx to the expansion that maniacs adds).
